links.comparator_used: Standard-of-care batch reading workflow (delayed radiologist interpretation after the patient left) with no AI prioritization
links.outcome: Time to additional imaging (TA) and time to biopsy diagnosis (TB)
links.effect: Control mean TA 25.6 days vs experimental 19.1 days (25% reduction, ΔTA = -6.4 days, p<0.001). Control mean TB 55.9 days vs experimental 39.2 days (30% reduction, ΔTB = -16.8 days, p=0.003). In AI-prioritized participants, mean TA was 3.5 days (86% shorter) and mean TB 30.2 days (46% shorter). All 6 cancers were prioritized by AI.
links.tradeoff: AI prioritized 29% of cases vs the 14% expected from retrospective testing, so more immediate reads were needed than planned. A radiologist was unavailable within 30 minutes for 6% (8/131) of prioritized cases. Same-visit imaging was not offered to 15% (5/33) for operational reasons, and 14% (4/28) declined it. Recall rate was 17.0% vs 14.3% (p=0.36, not significant). Immediate reads can disrupt workflow, and radiologists reported discomfort reading AI-prioritized cases as normal.
links.quote: The AI-modified workflow resulted in significantly shortened diagnostic delays (Fig. 3 ).

design_hint: AI triage prioritization for same-visit radiologist reading and diagnostic workup
